title: PostgreSQL Foreign Keys with ON DELETE CASCADE: Lock Cascade Hazards
realWorldScenario: A social commerce app uses `ON DELETE CASCADE` across 6 levels of relational hierarchy (`users` -> `posts` -> `comments` -> `reactions` -> `audit_events`). A user deletes their account, and the resulting cascading delete locks 250,000 rows across 8 tables, causing a database-wide deadlock storm.
questionStatement: Analyze the locking behavior and transaction risks of deep `ON DELETE CASCADE` chains in PostgreSQL. Why do cascading deletes cause long-running lock retention and deadlocks? What architectural alternatives (soft deletes, asynchronous background deletion workers) eliminate cascade locking hazards?
expectedConcepts: Single-transaction lock accumulation across entire relation hierarchy
All row locks held until COMMIT
Deadlocks with concurrent writes to descendant tables
Lack of throttling/batching in native database cascades
Soft delete + asynchronous chunked background deletion worker
hints: How long are locks held during an ON DELETE CASCADE transaction?
Can you pause or batch an ON DELETE CASCADE halfway through?
How do soft deletes decouple user experience from data cleanup?
